quarterly_data.signal: Northrop Grumman 10-Q (Q2 2026): significant second-quarter new awards also included $4.3 billion for restricted programs, $1.0 billion for F-35, $0.8 billion for Glide Phase Interceptor (GPI) and $0.7 billion for Multi-role Electronically Scanned Array (MESA); year-to-date net awards totaled $29.8 billion. Backlog of $104,692 million ($45,945 million funded) by segment: Defense Systems $34,678 million (+25 percent in 2026), Space Systems $26,981 million (+3 percent), Aeronautics Systems $24,568 million (+7 percent), Mission Systems $18,465 million. Under its first-quarter 2026 agreement with the U.S. Air Force to expand production capacity and increase the B-21 production rate, Northrop agreed to sell the Air Force an aircraft previously planned as a company-owned test asset, accelerating the LRIP delivery schedule without changing the number of LRIP aircraft.
quarterly_data.figure: GPI $0.8 billion; MESA $0.7 billion; YTD net awards $29.8 billion; Defense Systems backlog $34,678 million (+25 percent)

quarterly_data.signal: Northrop Grumman 10-Q (Q2 2026): sales to the U.S. government were $9,227 million (85 percent) and international sales $1,543 million (14 percent, versus $1,401 million); product sales $8.81 billion, up 6.7 percent, while service sales were $2.07 billion, down 1.2 percent. Space Systems Q2 sales were $2,753 million with operating income of $236 million (versus $280 million), including net unfavorable EAC adjustments of $91 million; Q2 capital expenditures were $302 million.
